analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Risk appetite collapse and the Outlook for 2027
key_insights: Markets had a major risk-off rotation last week with global equities entering a correction and bonds rallying.
GS stays modestly pro-risk for 2027 and favours greater balance across and within assets. Overweight equities and government bonds, Underweight credit, Neutral commodities and cash.

The valuation de-rating of recent months improves asymmetry for equities into 2027. A fading AI capex impulse and weaker earnings growth tailwinds likely mean lower risk-adjusted equity returns with higher volatility.

Higher starting real yields improve prospective bond returns. Easing inflation should make equity-bond correlations more negative, so bonds can better buffer equity weakness. This strengthens the case for balance with bonds.

Within equities GS favours diversification across styles, sectors and themes to balance Tech/AI-heavy benchmarks. It prefers equities to credit because of tight spreads, releveraging and rising supply.
US consumer demand was stronger than expected. October core retail sales rose 0.6% mom vs economists' 0.2% forecast, lifting Q4 GDP tracking to 2.4%.
FOMC minutes showed most participants expect further tightening. Asian central banks shifted more hawkishly. UK data showed softer labour demand but resilient consumption.
Key data this week are US core PCE on Wednesday and Euro area PMIs.

GS argues a 2027 peak in nominal and earnings growth need not end the bull market. Global real GDP growth is expected at 2.8%, and equities historically keep rising after nominal and earnings growth peak if real growth holds, especially with easing inflation and policy.

Risk Appetite Indicator fell to -1 at Friday's close. Readings near or below -2 have a hit ratio above 90% for positive S&P 500 returns over 6-12m, but the RAI has seldom reached -2 without a recession narrative.

Near-term risks remain elevated: AI concerns, renewed energy shocks, more aggressive Fed tightening and fiscal concerns. Selective hedges against equity downside and energy/rate upside remain attractive.
GS forecasts S&P 500 at 8300 (3m), 8500 (6m) and 8700 (12m) from 6910. US 10y yield forecast is 4.65% at 12m from 4.92%. Brent is forecast at 80 at 12m and gold at 4610.
Cross-asset implied vol is elevated: S&P 500 3m ATM implied vol is 24.7 (93rd percentile) and MSCI EM is 32.9 (98th percentile).
